lessons.name: Filtering, duplication and contamination
lessons.shortName: Filtering, duplication and contamination
lessons.role: Distinguish exact duplicates, approximate matches and evaluation contamination using explicit document families.
lessons.description: Duplicate detection defines an equivalence or similarity rule over content; it does not directly measure whether that content is true or useful. Raw-byte identity, normalized-text identity and overlap between token shingles can produce different groups. A group must be assigned to a split before its members are sampled, otherwise paraphrases or mirrors can leak across a nominal document split. Removing repeated data also changes exposure and source balance. A false merge discards distinct information, while a missed duplicate can overrepresent one source. The appropriate audit records both kinds of error on reviewed examples and measures downstream effects at a fixed token budget.
mechanism: Preserve original bytes and source identity before normalization.
Compute exact equality and a declared shingle similarity separately.
Form document-family groups, inspect borderline pairs, and assign whole groups to train, development or final.
Count unique retained families, mistaken merges and cross-split matches with separate denominators.
lessons.learningObjective: Distinguish exact duplicates, approximate matches and evaluation contamination using explicit document families.
lessons.engineeringExample: Authored documents A and B have shingle sets {red, square, left} and {red, square, right}. Their intersection has 2 items and union 4, so Jaccard similarity is 0.5. A threshold of 0.5 merges them even though left and right encode a different answer. Two other files with identical normalized text but different whitespace are exact normalized duplicates. Of 12 input files, retaining 9 representatives means a 25% file reduction; it says nothing by itself about token reduction or correctness.
lessons.evidenceNotes: Mode: worked example. Nonempty shingle union; exact set arithmetic. Threshold and authored semantic labels are teaching choices, not a universal deduplication rule. lessons.role: Calculate expected exposure per source and distinguish it from one finite seeded draw.
lessons.description: A training mixture is a probability distribution over available data, not a statement that every unique token is seen once. Sampling without replacement within an epoch has a different cursor contract. Changing mixture weights changes the learning objective in expectation; it also changes which domains consume a fixed budget. Allocate a fixed draw budget by source probability.
Divide expected draws by pool size to obtain expected epochs.
Inspect realized source counts and repeated examples for a specified RNG seed; do not replace them with their expectation.

lessons.name: Packing documents and masking valid targets
lessons.shortName: Packing documents and masking valid targets
lessons.role: Draw document and target masks, then reconstruct the loss denominator of a packed batch.
lessons.description: Packing places multiple sequences into fixed storage rows. Padding utilization, permission to attend across documents and permission to train on a target are three distinct choices. A causal mask blocks future inputs; a document mask can additionally block earlier tokens from another packed document. A target mask decides which shifted next-token predictions contribute to the objective. These masks need not be identical. Treating padding or the first token of an unrelated document as an ordinary target can change the objective even when the row has the expected shape.
mechanism: Write each document with its boundary marker and shift input/target positions explicitly.
Mark causal visibility and optional same-document visibility separately.
Exclude padding and any deliberately excluded boundary targets.
Sum all included losses before dividing by the total number of included targets.
lessons.learningObjective: Draw document and target masks, then reconstruct the loss denominator of a packed batch.
lessons.engineeringExample: One sequence contributes two valid target losses, 1 and 3 nats; another contributes five losses of 1 nat each. Token-mean loss is (1+3+5)/7=9/7=1.285714 nats. Averaging sequence means gives (2+1)/2=1.5 nats. Packing the rows into one buffer does not justify switching denominators. If a row has eight slots but only seven valid shifted targets, dividing by eight reports 1.125 and understates the objective.

lessons.name: Synthetic supervision and selection loops
lessons.shortName: Synthetic supervision and selection loops
lessons.role: Track a generated example through verification and selection without converting acceptance into ground truth.
lessons.description: Synthetic supervision has a lineage: a generator produces a candidate, a verifier or judge assigns a signal, and a selection rule decides whether to train on it. Each stage can introduce a different bias. Repeating a generator’s answer does not create independent evidence, and selecting only accepted outputs can hide the verifier’s blind spots. Generation seeds, prompts, model identities and verifier versions therefore belong to the dataset record. Final evaluation needs independently specified cases and scoring rules, rather than the same filter that selected training material.
mechanism: Retain rejected candidates as an audit sample alongside accepted examples.
Evaluate an independent reference on a bounded problem where the answer is actually computable.
Separate selection rate, precision among accepted examples and coverage of problem types.
Compare the trained model on a reserved task family; selection statistics are not model-quality measurements.
lessons.learningObjective: Track a generated example through verification and selection without converting acceptance into ground truth.
lessons.engineeringExample: Four authored candidates answer 2+2: 4, 5, 4 and 6. A faulty verifier accepts even numbers, so it accepts three candidates, including the wrong 6. Selection rate is 3/4; correctness among accepted candidates is 2/3. Deduplicating identical problem/answer pairs leaves {4,6}, whose correctness is 1/2. This denominator change reveals why duplicate correct answers can make a selected corpus look more reliable.

lessons.name: A differentiable computation graph
lessons.shortName: A differentiable computation graph
lessons.role: Accumulate every branch contribution to a reused parameter and check it by finite differences.
lessons.description: A forward computation creates intermediate values. Reverse-mode differentiation traverses the dependency graph backward, multiplying each incoming derivative by the local derivative and adding contributions where paths meet. Reusing one parameter in several operations creates several paths to the loss; its final gradient is their sum. The optimizer acts only after these derivatives have been computed. This distinction lets a learner locate an incorrect derivative independently of an incorrect update rule. Numerical finite differences provide a separate local check, although their accuracy depends on step size and smoothness.
mechanism: Save the forward operands required by local derivative rules.
Seed the scalar loss derivative with one.
Traverse operations in reverse dependency order and add, rather than overwrite, shared-input gradients.
Compare selected parameter derivatives with central differences while holding every other input fixed.

lessons.name: Gradient accumulation under a fixed global objective
lessons.shortName: Gradient accumulation under a fixed global objective
lessons.role: Recover a full-batch gradient from unequal target counts before clipping or stepping.
lessons.description: Gradient accumulation is a way to evaluate one global objective through several smaller forward/backward passes. Equivalence requires the same parameters for all those passes and the same weighting of included targets. Averaging two microbatch means equally silently changes the objective when their target counts differ. Optimizer steps between microbatches change the parameters at which later derivatives are evaluated. Nonlinear operations such as norm clipping also fail to commute with accumulation. Randomness, stateful layers and rounding add further limits to exact equivalence.
mechanism: Freeze the current weights across all microbatches in the update.
Retain each microbatch loss sum and valid-target count.
Add gradient sums and divide once by the global target denominator.
Clip the resulting global gradient once, then make exactly one optimizer step.
lessons.learningObjective: Recover a full-batch gradient from unequal target counts before clipping or stepping.
lessons.engineeringExample: Two valid targets yield mean scalar gradient 3; five yield mean gradient −1. The global mean is (2×3+5×(−1))/7=1/7. Equally averaging microbatch means gives 1 and is wrong. If each local mean is clipped to magnitude 1 first, the weighted result becomes (2−5)/7=−3/7, even reversing the sign. At weight 2 and SGD rate 0.7, the correct single update produces 1.9.
lessons.evidenceNotes: Mode: worked example. All gradients evaluated at the same weights with the same stochastic choices needed for equivalence. lessons.description: A reward model can assign scalar scores to candidate responses and fit observed pairwise preferences through their score differences. lessons.role: Separate generated action horizon, executed prefix and replanning interval.
lessons.description: A diffusion action policy generates a sequence of future commands conditioned on observations. Receding-horizon execution applies only a prefix, then receives new observations and generates another sequence. The prediction horizon and action-execution horizon are therefore different parameters. Executing a longer prefix reduces replanning frequency but delays reactions to disturbances. Inference latency also consumes part of the control budget and must be measured or explicitly assumed. Diffusion Policy studies this structure; the scalar command sequence here is a worked control trace, not a trained denoising policy.
mechanism: Record the observation time and generate an action chunk under a declared policy identity.
Execute only the selected prefix with an explicit command/period convention.
Observe disturbances and update the next planning state.
Compare closed-loop and open-loop outcomes while separating assumed inference delay from actual transition arithmetic.
